derivation: or אַשֻּׁר; from H833 (אָשַׁר) in the sense of going;

occurrences.text: My foot hath held his steps, his way have I kept, and not declined.
If my step hath turned out of the way, and mine heart walked after mine eyes, and if any blot hath cleaved to mine hands;
Hold up my goings in thy paths, that my footsteps slip not.
They have now compassed us in our steps: they have set their eyes bowing down to the earth;
The law of his God is in his heart; none of his steps shall slide.
Our heart is not turned back, neither have our steps declined from thy way;
But as for me, my feet were almost gone; my steps had well nigh slipped.

source: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890) and Concise Dictionaries (1894), public domain; JSON by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA).
